fact: UNDP Niger says the commune urbaine of Diffa put Naneye Yarda into service on 11 December 2025, a system covering the whole tax cycle: a digital census of taxable establishments by agents with tablets, automatic tax calculation, tax notices with QR codes, and payment by electronic terminals carried by tax collectors.

UNDP Niger says Diffa is the first region outside the capital to deploy the full digitalisation of municipal taxation; it gives no count of communes in the country, and the document names no other commune outside Niamey.
UNDP Niger reports the commune urbaine of Diffa commissioned the Naneye Yarda municipal tax system on 11 December 2025, replacing manual collection with incomplete taxpayer files.

Le Sahel quotes the City of Niamey's delegated administrator saying 50 field agents with mobile devices had geolocated over 2,000 taxpayers, and that municipal tax payments through Al Izza and Nita were integrated with real-time revenue tracking and an automated audit of each transaction; the article is dated 2025-01-29 and gives the launch as a Monday.
Le Sahel reports the platform launched in the City of Niamey only; it names no other commune.

Le Sahel says the City of Niamey launched Naneye Yarda under its 2025-2027 strategic plan, with the national information society agency ANSI building the architecture; it names no donor or budget line.

Journal du Niger reports that on 21 August 2025 the City of Niamey's delegated administrator received 100 electronic payment terminals from the Programme Village Intelligent, to speed collection of public funds; the report states the terminals were handed over, not that they are in use or what they record.
ANP reports that on 3 October 2024 the City of Niamey launched the Naney Yarda platform, which is to digitise the census of taxpayers with geolocation, to determine the taxable base across the city.
ANP reports that Naney Yarda was launched for the City of Niamey alone on 3 October 2024; no other commune is mentioned and no count of taxpayers recorded is given.
The Niamey delegated administrator calls Naney Yarda the main pillar of the city's 2025-2027 strategic plan, and the national information society agency ANSI is named as technology partner.
